quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: How do you enter a freeway?

options.text: Signal, yield to other cars, and enter at the same speed as the traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly so you can check the traffic.
Always come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to other cars, and enter at the same speed as the traffic.
questions.explanation: Signal before merging. Enter at the same speed as the traffic around you. Always yield to other cars when entering a road.

questions.question: If you get stranded in a snowstorm, what should you do?

options.text: Get out of the car and walk for help.
Lie down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in your car. You are most likely to be found if you stay in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car. You are most likely to be found if you stay in your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay in your car and wait for help. Rescue workers will find you more easily if you stay in your vehicle. Walking in a snowstorm is dangerous.

questions.question: What does a solid white line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: Checking your blind spot by turning your head before changing lanes or merging is:

options.text: A bad driving habit.
A good driving habit.
Unnecessary.
Not necessary if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: Always check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed when roads are wet.
Use tires with the correct air pressure.
Replace worn-out tires.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires slide on water. Low tire pressure, worn tire tread, and speeding all increase hydroplaning risk.

questions.question: Driving while distracted:

options.text: Is never dangerous.
Usually slows your reaction time to hazards.
Usually makes you drive faster.
Is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually slows your reaction time to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions slow how quickly you react to traffic and hazards. Distracted driving is never safe.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Four-lane traffic ahead.
Divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.
Intersection ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that two-way traffic is coming.

questions.question: Which traffic light means you should slow down and be careful at an intersection?

options.text: A flashing yellow light
A flashing red light
A solid yellow light
A solid red light

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, be careful, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When is it safe to pass on a two-way, two-lane road?

options.text: When you can see the road ahead clearly.
When you can get back to your lane before oncoming cars reach you.
When your car can go fast enough to pass.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Safe passing requires three things: clear view of the road ahead, ability to return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and a car that can go fast enough to pass. Only pass where it is legal and safe.

questions.question: When should you use one-hand steering?

options.text: When turning the wheel during normal driving.
When avoiding a hazard at high speed.
When turning the wheel at low speeds.
When backing up or using controls like signals, radio, or wipers.

questions.correctAnswerText: When backing up or using controls like signals, radio, or wipers.
questions.explanation: Use one hand only when backing up or when you need to reach controls like wipers, signals, or lights. Keep both hands on the wheel otherwise.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from the car in front of you.
Drive in the right lane only.
Drive slower than the traffic around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance gives you time to react to problems ahead without emergency braking. Emergency stops can cause the car behind you to crash into your vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn left.
No left turn.
No U-turn.
Truck route to the left.

questions.explanation: This sign tells you that left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What do diagonal stripes sloping downward to the left on a barricade mean?

options.text: You must stop.
You should steer to the right.
You should steer to the left.
You should drive straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should steer to the left.
questions.explanation: Diagonal stripes on a barricade show drivers which way to go. Stripes sloping downward to the right mean steer right. Stripes sloping downward to the left mean steer left.

questions.question: What is the "No zone"?

options.text: The blind spots around a truck or bus where other vehicles cannot be seen.
A special speed zone.
A roadway with rules about stereo volume.
A television show that replaced The Twilight Zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spots around a truck or bus where other vehicles cannot be seen.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on both sides, in the rear, and in the front. Cars in these areas cannot be seen by the truck or bus driver. These blind spots are called the "No zone."

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, what must other drivers be prepared for?

options.text: Large trucks need more distance to stop.
Large trucks need less distance to stop.
Large trucks are quieter.
Large trucks move faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks need more distance to stop.
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles. Stay where the truck driver can see you and where your view of the road is not blocked by the truck.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Drive slowly and carefully.
Do not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to see the road and objects ahead better.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Fog reduces your ability to see other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, drive slowly and carefully. Do not use high beams. Low beams work better in foggy conditions.

questions.question: What do crossbuck signs mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
School zone ahead.
No passing zone.
Hospital ahead.

questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs warn drivers that trains cross at this location. You must yield to trains and never try to drive across the tracks ahead of a train.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on wet roads?

options.text: Your tires grip the road less effectively as you drive faster.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
The road becomes more slippery as you slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires grip the road less effectively as you drive faster.
questions.explanation: As you drive faster on wet roads, your tires cannot remove water from the pavement as effectively. At high speeds, your tires may lose their grip entirely, causing you to hydroplane and slide on the water.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see which signal?

options.text: A flashing red light.
A steady yellow light.
A yellow arrow.
A flashing yellow light.

questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, look both ways, and only proceed when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Tow-away zone.
Steep downgrade.
Roadwork ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign warns you to be careful because the road may be wet and slippery.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Keep a safe distance from the car ahead.
Get closer to the car ahead.
Stop completely before changing lanes.
Quickly swerve in and out of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance from the car ahead.
questions.explanation: Keep a safe distance from the car in front of you when changing lanes. Check your mirrors and blind spots to make sure no cars are in your way or entering the lane you want.

questions.question: Which statement about emergency vehicles is true?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and flashing lights.
They can use a loudspeaker to give instructions.
They can follow each other closely.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to police cars, fire trucks, and ambulances when they use a siren or horn and flashing red or blue lights. Follow any instructions from their loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so only proceed when you are sure the road is clear.

questions.question: You are waiting in a line at a stop sign. The cars ahead pass through. There is no traffic coming. What must you do?

options.text: You can go through without stopping again.
You must stop at the stop sign or stop line again before going.
You can roll slowly past the stop sign.
You can follow the car ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop at the stop sign or stop line again before going.
questions.explanation: You must always come to a complete stop at a stop sign and check for traffic before moving. Do not skip stopping just because other cars are moving.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Speed up.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Intersection ahead.
Four-way stop ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is coming. Watch carefully for cars crossing your path.

questions.question: When driving where children are playing, what should you expect?

options.text: They know when it is safe to cross.
They will stop at the curb before crossing.
They might run in front of you without looking.
They will not cross unless an adult is with them.

questions.correctAnswerText: They might run in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be extra careful where children play. Children may not understand danger and could run into the street without looking.

questions.question: Which drugs can affect your driving?

options.text: Allergy medicine
Marijuana
Cold medicine
All of these

questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair your driving. This includes illegal drugs and legal prescription or over-the-counter medicines. Driving while impaired by any drug is a crime.

questions.question: Which must you obey over the others?

options.text: A red light
A police officer
A stop sign
A flashing red light

questions.explanation: A police officer's directions take priority over all signs and signals. This also applies to fire police, road workers directing traffic, and school crossing guards.

questions.question: What does the speed limit sign show?

options.text: A suggested speed only.
The exact speed you must drive to avoid a ticket.
The maximum safe speed in good road and weather conditions.
The maximum safe speed in all conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed in good road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: The speed limit is the fastest you can legally drive on that road. You may need to drive slower than the limit depending on weather and road conditions.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private driveway?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn other drivers.
Back part of your car onto the roadway to alert drivers.
Speed out to blend with traffic.
Let pedestrians and traffic on the road go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians and traffic on the road go first.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must give the right-of-way to pedestrians and all traffic on the roadway.

questions.question: When can you go through a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check for cross traffic
After stopping completely and making sure it is safe
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection
After slowing to 10 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: After stopping completely and making sure it is safe
questions.explanation: Stop before entering any intersection with a stop sign. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before the intersection and go only when it is safe.

questions.question: It starts to rain while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Drive faster than other cars.
Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Slow down.
Drive very close behind the car in front of you.

questions.explanation: When it rains hard, you cannot see as well. Slow down and turn on your headlights so other drivers can see you. If the rain is so heavy that you cannot see, pull over to the side of the road and stop until it clears.

questions.question: The space you need to cross traffic depends on:

options.text: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
Whether there is a stop sign.
Whether you use your turn signals.
The cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on the road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Compared to driving during the day, driving at night is:

options.text: Less dangerous.
About the same danger.
More dangerous.
Easier on your eyes.

questions.explanation: Driving at night is more dangerous than driving during the day. It is harder to see in the dark. Headlights from other cars can blind you. More tired drivers and drivers under the influence are on the road at night.

questions.question: Traffic lanes going in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.explanation: Solid white lines separate lanes going in the same direction and mark the right edge of the road. Broken white lines also separate lanes going the same direction and can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate lanes going in opposite directions.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is against the law to drive around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop when a flagger tells you to stop at a railroad crossing.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red lights and gates.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices tell you to. Not all crossings have lights or gates. It is against the law to drive around lowered railroad gates.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light has the same rules as:

options.text: A slow sign.
A yield sign.
A stop sign.
An intersection sign.

questions.explanation: When you see a flashing red light, you must stop and let all other traffic go first.

questions.question: Drivers should use hand-over-hand steering:

options.text: When turning the wheel during normal driving.
When avoiding a hazard at high speed.
When turning the wheel at low speeds.
When backing up, using signals, or adjusting the radio.

questions.correctAnswerText: When turning the wheel at low speeds.
questions.explanation: Use hand-over-hand steering when turning at low speeds, such as at an intersection or when parking. Place your left hand between 8 and 9 o'clock on the wheel and your right hand between 3 and 4 o'clock.

questions.question: In snowy weather, your following distance should:

options.text: Increase.
Decrease.
Stay the same.
Not matter.

questions.explanation: In bad driving conditions, slow down and stay farther away from the car in front of you. It takes much longer to stop on icy roads than on dry roads.

questions.question: A steady green light means you:

options.text: Must slow down and prepare to stop.
Must stop and check for oncoming traffic.
May drive through if the road is clear.
May not turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: May drive through if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can drive through the intersection if the road is clear. You may also turn right or left unless a sign says you cannot. When turning, yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is one who:

options.text: Looks at objects off the road or daydreams while driving.
Stares at a passenger while talking during driving.
Only watches the car ahead.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by looking at passengers, searching for things in your car, reading, sightseeing, or daydreaming. Keep scanning the road, check your mirrors often, and look at your dashboard regularly. These safe habits will keep you attentive while driving.
